ecommerce.description: E-commerce REST API built as a learning and portfolio project, focused on backend organization, data validation, and relational persistence.
ecommerce.problemDesc: An e-commerce workflow needs to keep users, catalog, orders, and stock consistent. This API brings these operations together through organized endpoints and applies core rules on the server instead of trusting values sent by the client.
ecommerce.whatDesc: A REST API built with NestJS and Fastify, using PostgreSQL for persistence and Prisma for data access. Modules are separated by domain, and services depend on repository contracts to keep business logic separate from persistence implementation.
featureItems: CRUD for users, categories, and products
Filter products by category and partial name
Create and retrieve orders, with optional user filtering
Server-side total calculation and unit-price snapshot at purchase time
Stock deduction when creating an order and restoration on cancellation
Data and environment validation with Zod
Password hashing with Argon2 and global exception handling
ecommerce.architectureDesc: The application is organized into domain modules and uses the Repository pattern to separate services from persistence. Order operations use transactions to keep order and stock data consistent.
ecommerce.flow: Controller → Service → Abstract Repository → Prisma Repository → PostgreSQL
ecommerce.limitationsDesc: The project does not implement authentication or authorization. It was built to demonstrate backend concepts and should not be used in production with real data without the necessary protections.
ecommerce.endpointsDesc: Main operations available in the API, grouped by resource. Check the interactive documentation for parameters and response formats.
ecommerce.rulesDesc: Order totals are calculated on the server, unit prices are preserved at purchase time, and stock changes are handled within transactions. Stock is restored only when an order is successfully cancelled, preventing duplicate restocking.

bookshelf.description: Full Stack application for managing a personal reading list, allowing users to add books, track reading progress, and record ratings.
bookshelf.objectiveDesc: The project was developed to deepen frontend development knowledge, particularly with React and Next.js, while gaining practical experience integrating independent applications. It also involved working with HTTP communication, form management, data validation, and frontend-backend integration.
bookshelf.problemDesc: Keeping a reading list organized can become challenging as new books are added. Bookshelf centralizes this management in a single application, allowing users to track reading status and keep book information organized.
bookshelf.whatDesc: A Full Stack application composed of two independent applications: a frontend built with Next.js and a REST API developed with NestJS. It allows users to manage a personal book collection through creation, retrieval, updating, and deletion operations.
featureItems: Create, list, update, and delete books
Register book titles, authors, reading status, and ratings
Filter books by reading status through URL parameters
Reusable form for creating and editing books
Loading states and error handling in book listings
Data validation with Zod on both frontend and backend
Interactive API documentation with OpenAPI and Scalar
bookshelf.frontendDesc: Built with Next.js 16, React 19, and TypeScript, using the App Router for page organization. The interface uses Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui components. Forms are managed with React Hook Form and validated with Zod. HTTP requests are centralized in a service layer using Axios.
bookshelf.backendDesc: REST API developed with NestJS 12 and Fastify, using PostgreSQL for persistence and Prisma for database access. The application is organized by domain modules and uses the Repository Pattern to separate business logic from persistence implementation. Data validation is handled by Zod integrated with NestJS StandardSchemaValidationPipe.
bookshelf.endpointsDesc: The API provides CRUD operations for book management, as well as filtering capabilities based on reading status.
bookshelf.architectureDesc: The frontend and API are independent applications. The frontend uses a service layer to centralize HTTP requests, while the backend organizes responsibilities by module and uses the Repository Pattern to decouple services from persistence.
bookshelf.flow: Next.js → Service Layer → Axios → NestJS Controller → Service → Repository → Prisma → PostgreSQL
bookshelf.limitationsDesc: The project does not implement authentication or authorization. The book listing does not include pagination, and automated tests specific to the book module have not yet been implemented. Therefore, the application should not be used in a public environment with data requiring access control until the necessary security measures are implemented.
